name: Wolf Hollow - North American Wolf Foundation
Halibut Point State Park
description:
AI: One of the most dramatic coastal parks in Massachusetts. Built around an abandoned granite quarry overlooking the Atlantic, the park offers sweeping ocean views, rocky shoreline scenery, and excellent sunset spots.

Why go: one of the most beautiful ocean viewpoints in the state.
Must visit.

name: Frederick Law Olmsted National Historic Site
John Fitzgerald Kennedy National Historic Site
Lowell National Historical Park Visitor Center
Mill Girls and Immigrants Exhibit (Lowell NHP)
Minute Man National Historical Park
description: At Minute Man National Historical Park the opening battle of the Revolution is brought to life as visitors explore the battlefields and structures associated with April 19, 1775, and witness the American revolutionary spirit through the writings of the Concord authors.

name: The Wayside Home of Authors
description: Over more than three hundred years, The Wayside and its families witnessed and influenced both Concord's and America's recorded history. In 1775 the Wayside was home to Samuel Whitney the muster master for Concord's minute men and a delegate to the Provincial Congress. In the 19th century famed authors Louisa May Alcott, Nathaniel Hawthorne, and Margaret Sidney (Harriet Lothrop) lived at this incredible site.

name: New Bedford Whaling National Historical Park
Faneuil Hall Visitor Center
description: For 275 years and counting, Faneuil Hall has hosted meetings, protests, celebrations, ceremonies, and debates. Because Revolutionary-era meetings and protests took place so frequently at the hall, successive generations continued to gather at the Hall in their own struggles over the meaning and legacy of American liberty. Abolitionists, women's suffragists, and labor unionists name just the largest of groups who have held protests, meetings, and debates at Faneuil Hall.

name: Old State House
description: Constructed in 1713, the Old State House was the center of royal government in the Massachusetts Bay colony and the focal point for many of the Revolution’s most dramatic events. It was here that the Boston Massacre occurred in 1770.

name: Old North Church
description: “One if by land, and two if by sea!” With two lanterns shining from its steeple on April 18, 1775, Old North Church lit the way for the American Revolution. Come and explore 300 years of history at Boston’s oldest church building. Old North is a family-friendly Freedom Trail destination and active Episcopal Church. Join the warm and welcoming congregation for worship on Sundays. AI: The church of "one if by land, two if by sea" fame maintains a guild of change-ringers who practice the complex English art of ringing tower bells in mathematical patterns. If you can time your visit to hear them (Saturday mornings, typically), it's a haunting sonic experience that connects directly to 18th-century Boston.

name: USS Cassin Young
description: Built in 1943 in San Pedro, California, USS Cassin Young is one of 175 Fletcher-class destroyers built during World War II. She engaged in seven Pacific battles during World War II, survived two Kamikaze hits, and served another full decade beyond her expected lifetime.

name: Dorchester Heights
description:
The Dorchester Heights Monument commemorates the fortification of those Heights on the evening of March 4, 1776. After months of planning, George Washington ordered continental forces and local volunteers to stealthily fortify this location with cannon. This military operation led British forces to evacuate Boston two weeks later, on March 17, 1776.

In 1898, the General Court of Massachusetts commissioned a monument to stand on the remaining hill of the Heights. Designed by the architectural firm of Peabody and Stearns, the white marble Georgian revival tower commemorates the 1776 victory. Dorchester Heights' historical significance and the development of the surrounding community vividly reflect the history and growth of the city of Boston.

name: Black Heritage Trail
description:
The Museum of African American History is New England’s largest museum dedicated to preserving, conserving and interpreting the contributions of African Americans. In Boston and Nantucket, the Museum has preserved two historic sites and two Black Heritage Trails that tell the story of organized black communities from the Colonial Period through the 19th century.

Highlights
Here are some of the "must see" items at Museum of African American History.

African Meeting House
Abiel Smith School
Black Heritage Trail

name: Spectacle Island
description: check out sea glass beaches and collection in the visitors center. Trash escaped from a landfill to fill beaches with all kinds of treasure.

name: Longfellow House-Washington's Headquarters National Historic Site
description: One of America's most historic homes also holds a startling literary legacy.

name: Saugus Iron Works National Historic Site
description:
AI: One of the most fascinating industrial heritage sites in the United States. This was the first integrated ironworks in colonial America (1640s), producing tools and iron products for the young colonies. Today the National Park Service operates reconstructed furnaces, mills, and workshops powered by waterwheels.

Why go: one of the best places in the country to understand early American industry.
Must visit.

name: Madonna Queen of the Universe Shrine
description: A 35-foot copper Madonna overlooks the harbor from East Boston, built in 1954 as a memorial to immigrants. The grounds are peaceful, the views unexpected.

name: MIT List Visual Arts Center
description:
AI: MIT’s contemporary art museum often hosts experimental exhibitions that engage with technology, architecture, and research. The programming is intellectually ambitious and frequently features artists at the forefront of contemporary practice.

Why go: One of the most interesting small contemporary art spaces in the Boston area.

name: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
description:
AI: A wildly atmospheric museum created by collector Isabella Stewart Gardner inside a Venetian-style palace. The galleries remain arranged exactly as Gardner installed them in 1903—paintings, sculptures, tapestries, and furniture packed into richly decorated rooms surrounding a spectacular indoor courtyard garden.

The museum is also famous for the 1990 art heist, when thieves stole masterpieces by Vermeer, Rembrandt, and Degas that have never been recovered.

Why go: One of the most distinctive museum experiences in America.

name: Harvard Art Museums
description: forbes pigment collection - The thousands of shades on display — some toxic, others impossibly rare — are a library of more than just color.

name: Paul S. Russell, MD Museum of Medical History and Innovation at Massachusetts General Hospital
description:
The Paul S. Russell, MD Museum of Medical History and Innovation presents the 200-year evolution of health care and medicine at Massachusetts General Hospital. The museum's exhibits cover various topics including the evolution of health care, laboratory and clinical research, and patient and family support.

Highlights
Here are some of the "must see" items at Russell Museum of Medical History and Innovation.

MGH Nurse's Charm 1937
Richardson, M. H., MD, Scalpel Set
Amputatiion Kit, Hayward, George, M.D.

name: Norman B. Leventhal Map & Education Center
description: AI:  Housed in the Boston Public Library's McKim Building (itself worth the visit), this collection holds 200,000 maps and 5,000 atlases spanning five centuries. The rotating exhibitions reveal how cartography shaped empires and erased peoples. Free entry in one of America's great library buildings.

name: Forest Hills Cemetery
description: A beautiful Victorian-era cemetery, complete with a miniature village.

name: Boston Athenaeum
description: look for the skin book

name: Brook Farm Historic Site
description: Site of an experimental utopian community based on Transcendentalist and Unitarian thought.

name: Ether Dome
description: AI: On October 16, 1846, in this austere amphitheatre at Massachusetts General Hospital, a dentist administered ether while a surgeon removed a tumour from a patient's neck. The patient felt nothing. Modern anaesthesia was born. The dome remains almost unchanged – tiered wooden seats, natural light from above, an Egyptian mummy in the corner (don't ask). One of the most significant rooms in medical history, and you can simply walk in for free.

name: Franklin Park - Overlook Ruins
description: The often-overlooked ruins of one of the first buildings designed by famous landscape architect Frederick Olmsted.

name: Winthrop Lane
description: check for bricks - These whimsical works of art tell the story of the city's past and present.

name: King's Chapel
description: visit the crypt

name: Creek Square
description: This historic patch of real estate offers a glimpse of colonial Boston

name: The Harvard Museum of Natural History
description: AI: Everyone knows the Blaschka glass flowers, but fewer visitors seek out the marine invertebrates the same father-son team created for Harvard in the 1870s. Glass jellyfish, anemones, and octopi rendered with terrifying delicacy. They were scientific models; they look like fever dreams. In the Natural History Museum.

name: Modica Way
description: An alley way dedicated to graffiti and street art is a constantly changing street gallery.

name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
description: infinite corridor

name: Assabet River National Wildlife Refuge
description: In the middle of a New England forest sit the crumbling ruins of World War II-era ammunition storage bunkers.

name: Ford's Folly
description: This dam in the woods, built by Henry Ford with only manpower and oxen, holds no water and serves no purpose.

name: Newton City Hall
description: Battle dioramas in the Veterans Wing - These impressively detailed battle scenes depict the violence and tragedy of war in miniature.

name: Echo Bridge
description: A historic bridge with a lovely acoustic anomaly.

name: Quincy Quarries Reservation
description: From economic backbone of a community to deadly diving hole, these former stone quarries are now a park for rock climbers and graffiti artists.

name: Metropolitan Waterworks Museum
description: Beautiful steampunk ghosts of early Massachusetts.

name: Arthur & Elizabeth Schlesinger Library
description: huge culinary collection

name: Charles River Museum of Industry & Innovation
description: A steampunk wonderland that preserves America's history of industrial innovation.

name: Reflecting Pool at the Christian Science Plaza
The Vilna Shul
description:
The Vilna Shul, originally an Orthodox synagogue, was built in 1919 by immigrants primarily from Vilna, Lithuania. Today it is a historic landmark building located in historic Beacon Hill and home to a cultural center, community center, and living museum.

Highlights
Here are some of the "must see" items at Vilna Shul.

The cultural center

name: The West End Museum
description:
The West End Museum is a neighborhood museum dedicated to the collection, preservation, and interpretation of the history and culture of the West End of Boston. The history of the West End is one of a largely immigrant neighborhood displaced or destroyed by the 1958 and 1960 ‘Urban Renewal‘ campaigns.

Highlights
Here are some of the "must see" items at West End Museum.

The Last Tenement
The Middlesex Canal: Boston's First Big Dig
Leaving the River

name: Larz Anderson Auto Museum
description: AI: America's oldest car collection, housed in the 1888 carriage house of a Gilded Age estate. The vehicles belonged to diplomat Larz Anderson and his heiress wife Isabel, who simply kept buying new automobiles without selling the old ones. The result is an intimate, quirky museum spanning horseless carriages to early 20th-century luxury cars, displayed in a setting that feels like raiding a wealthy eccentric's garage.

name: SIMMONS Trustman Art Gallery
description:
Trustman Art Gallery is the gallery space for the Simmons College students of Art and Music. The gallery exhibits the work of professional artists and has a yearly exhibition of student work from the Department of Art and Music.

Highlights
Here are some of the "must see" items at Trustman Art Gallery at Simmons College.

The Painted Place: Mia Cross
20 Years of the Art of Grace Lin
All Good Things: Greg Lamarche

name: Shirley-Eustis House
description: The Shirley–Eustis House was built between 1747 and 1751 on 33 acres in Roxbury by William Shirley, Royal Governor of the Province of Massachusetts Bay. The orchards, gardens, and grounds are free and open to the public year-round, from dawn until dusk.

name: Berlin Wall Segment at Hult International School
BSA Space
description:
Boston Society of Architects (BSA) Space is Boston's only center dedicated to the exploration of architecture and design. The space hosts exhibitions on design and architecture, architecture cruises and walking tours, and other programs and events that foster exchange between design and construction.

Highlights
Here are some of the "must see" items at BSA Space.

Canstruction
New Visions of Designed Environments
IGBoston Snapshot

name: The Printing Office Of Edes And Gill
The Embrace
description: This bronze sculpture was inspired by a photograph of Martin Luther King Jr. and his wife embracing after he won the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Statue of Mary Dyer
description: Dedicated to a colonial woman who was hanged for being a Quaker.

name: The Liberty, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Boston
description: A luxury hotel constructed out of a former jail.

name: The BYTE Shop
description: This electronics repair store celebrates the history of computers.

name: Salada Tea Headquarters
description: The history of the tea trade is told in bas-relief on this historic pair of Boston doors.

name: Hincman’s Bench
description: From bench to vandalism to art, this silly prank seat was funny enough to become permanent.

name: The First Church of Christ, Scientist
description: This impressive Boston holy house is the American mecca for Christian scientists.

name: All Saints Way
description: "Mock all and sundry things, but leave the saints alone."  AI: A narrow alley off Battery Street transformed by one devoted resident into a dense shrine of saints' images, rosaries, photos, and Catholic ephemera. Hundreds of items cover every surface. It's folk art, it's devotion, it's wonderfully strange – and most visitors to the North End walk right past without noticing. Ring the bell if Peter Baldassari is home; he may invite you to add to the collection.

name: Dutch House
description: This Dutch-styled residential building was originally a cocoa company's World's Fair showpiece.

name: The Sports Museum
description: The Sports Museum is located in Boston's TD Garden, the home of the Boston Bruins and Boston Celtics. The exhibits celebrate the history and the character of sports in the Boston area, including the Boston Bruins, Boston Celtics, Boston Red Sox, New England Patriots, Boston Marathon, New England Revolution, boxing, college sports, and others.

name: Schoolmaster Hill
description: Ralph Waldo Emerson spent two years living here decades before it became a Frederick Law Olmsted-designed park

name: Calf Pasture Sewage Pumping Station
description: This beautiful architectural gem was the first waste treatment facility in Boston.

name: John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum
The Purple House
description: One man's psychedelic fence is painted with his cacophonous folk art musings on the world.

name: Longfellow Bridge Trophy Room
description: An anonymous art project beneath Longfellow Bridge where hundreds of trophies line the steel support beams.

name: The Brattle Theatre
description: One of the last remaining movie theatres in the country that features a rear-projection system.

name: Kendall Band
description: A three-piece musical sculpture installed between the subway tracks at Kendall Station near MIT.

name: John Harvard Statue
description: The statue of John Harvard isn't actually John Harvard—or even, technically, the founder of the school.

name: The Collection of Historical Scientific Instruments at the Putnam Gallery
description: contains massive World War II calculator that hearkens back to the days when "computer" was a job title.

name: Cambridge Spite House
description: This is the house that spite built.

name: Skinny House (Spite House) Boston, MA
description: Narrowest house in Boston.

name: Mount Auburn Cemetery
description: This peaceful Massachusetts graveyard was one of the first "garden-style" cemeteries in America.

name: Old Burial Ground
description: This cemetery served as the only official burial grounds in Cambridge for nearly 200 years.

name: MIT Edgerton Center
description: MIT students continue the legacy of beloved professor "Doc" Edgerton through learning by doing.

name: Lyman Estate Greenhouses, Historic New England
description: These beautiful garden buildings are among the oldest surviving greenhouses in the United States.

name: Metropolitan State Hospital
description: Once the largest public hospital for the mentally ill was also surrounded by controversy.

name: Armenian Museum of America
description: Large Massachusetts museum dedicated to Armenian history and culture.

name: Museum of Modern Renaissance
description: This former Masonic hall has been turned into an art project that uses even more metaphysical iconography.

name: Old Powder House
description: Rising 30 feet in the air atop Quarry Hill, the Old Powder House is the oldest stone building in the state of Massachusetts.

name: The Friend Smithsonian Museum
description: A home decorated by its owner with eye-catching and captivating assemblages of found objects

name: Shrine of Our Lady of Good Voyage
description:
Built in the 1950s to serve fishermen,
longshoremen, and their families, the Chapel
moved to a new site this year to better serve
local workers. The new chapel retains much of its
nautical heritage with a ceiling patterned after
the hull of a ship and walls inscribed with the
prayer “They that go down to the sea in ships,
that do business in great waters…” It is a beautiful
house of prayer, intimate in size, but majestic in
its elements

name: First Baptist Church of Boston
description:
Originally built for the Brattle Square Unitarian
congregation, this site demonstrates H. H.
Richardson’s first use of Romanesque forms.
The First Baptist Church purchased the
building in 1880. Built of Roxbury puddingstone
laid in random ashlar, the church features a
monumental tower topped by a decorative frieze
and corbelled arches. Notable are the tower
sculptures by Frederic Auguste Bartholdi; Hook
and Hastings Organ Opus 727, which includes
pipework from an English organ of 1792; and
Louis Comfort Tiffany's window “Saint John the
Divine.”

name: Gropius House
description: AI: The former home of Walter Gropius, founder of the Bauhaus school. Built in 1938, the house introduced European modernist design to American architecture. The clean lines, modern materials, and thoughtful integration with the landscape make it a landmark of 20th-century architecture.

name: Sacred Cod
description: AI: A five-foot wooden fish has hung in the Massachusetts State House since 1784, symbolizing the industry that built the colony. When Harvard pranksters "codnapped" it in 1933, the legislature refused to meet until it was recovered. Absurd, beloved, and genuinely historic – peek into the House of Representatives chamber to pay your respects.

name: Ancient and Honorable Artillery Company
description: AI: Founded in 1638, this is the oldest military organization in the Western Hemisphere, and their small museum in Faneuil Hall is crammed with centuries of martial ephemera. The kind of place that rewards curiosity.

name: Steaming Kettle
description: AI: This gilded kettle has hung over Scollay Square (now Government Center) since 1873, periodically emitting actual steam. Its capacity – 227 gallons, 2 quarts, 1 pint, and 3 gills – was the subject of a public guessing contest. Charming survivor of old commercial Boston.

name: North Bennet Street School
description: America's oldest trade school (1881) still teaches bookbinding, violin-making, and cabinet-making in its cramped North End quarters. Occasional tours and workshops offer glimpses of craftsmanship that's nearly vanished elsewhere.

name: Great Molasses Flood Plaque
description: AI: On January 15, 1919, a poorly constructed storage tank burst and sent 2.3 million gallons of molasses surging through the North End at 35 miles per hour. The wave, two stories high, killed 21 people, injured 150, and flattened buildings. Horses drowned. The harbour ran brown for months. It remains one of history's most improbable industrial disasters, and this small plaque near the Langone Recreation Center is the only marker. Locals claim you can still smell molasses on hot summer days. (They can't, but they'll tell you anyway.)

name: Copps Hill Burying Ground
description: AI: Bullet Marks on the Grave of Daniel Malcom – In Copp's Hill Burying Ground, British Redcoats used headstones for target practice during the siege of Boston. They were particularly enthusiastic about Malcom's stone, which defiantly proclaimed him "a true son of Liberty" and enemy of royal customs officers. The musket-ball pockmarks remain visible 250 years later – tangible Revolutionary rage you can touch.

name: Harvard Bridge
description: Everyone knows the Blaschka glass flowers, but fewer visitors seek out the marine invertebrates the same father-son team created for Harvard in the 1870s. Glass jellyfish, anemones, and octopi rendered with terrifying delicacy. They were scientific models; they look like fever dreams. In the Natural History Museum.

name: N52
description: The Tech Model Railroad club is an MIT student activity founded during the 1946-1947 school year, making TMRC one of the oldest clubs at MIT. This site contains information on the club, both past and present. There is information about the early days of the club, when we were located in building 20, and the current activities of the club in our current home, building N52, where we’ve been since 1997. If you’d like to visit the club, we’re usually happy to welcome visitors during our regular meetings, and hold an open house twice a year, when you can be sure that lots of trains will be running. MIT students are always welcome to visit and join the club.

name: Wadsworth House
description: AI: Wadsworth House Slavery Plaque – This yellow clapboard house on Harvard Yard is one of the university's oldest buildings. A 2016 plaque finally acknowledges the enslaved people who lived and worked here, part of Harvard's belated reckoning with its complicity in slavery.

name: Christ Church Cambridge
description: AI: George Washington's Pew – Christ Church Cambridge preserves the pew where Washington worshipped while commanding the Continental Army. The church itself is a handsome colonial survivor.

name: Hart Nautical Gallery
description: AI: MIT's collection of ship models, marine engineering artifacts, and naval architecture. Small but satisfying for maritime enthusiasts.

name: Taza Chocolate
description: AI: This Somerville chocolate maker produces stone-ground Mexican-style chocolate using traditional molinos. The factory tour is short, genuinely informative, and ends with generous samples of intensely gritty, boldly flavored discs. One of the better food tours in Greater Boston.

name: Neon Williams
description: AI: A working neon sign studio in Somerville where you can watch craftspeople bend glass tubes into glowing art. Niche but atmospheric.

name: Deer Island Wastewater Treatment Plant
description: Twelve 150-foot eggs dominate the harbor horizon, and yes, they process sewage. The MWRA runs occasional tours of this engineering marvel, and the guides are disarmingly proud of the facility that cleaned up Boston Harbor. Industrial tourism at its most wonderfully strange.

name: Mattapan
description: These candy-apple-red PCC streetcars from 1946 are among the oldest transit vehicles in regular service in America, rattling through working-class neighborhoods between Ashmont and Mattapan. Ride the entire line for a Boston experience no tourist brochure advertises.

name: Edward M. Kennedy Institute for the United States Senate
description: AI: Adjacent to the JFK Library, this interactive museum lets you roleplay as a senator, complete with mock floor debates and constituent meetings. Surprisingly engaging, even for the politically disenchanted. The replica Senate chamber alone is worth the visit.

name: Old Bear Dens
description: AI: In Franklin Park, the crumbling 1912 bear dens designed by the Olmsted firm are now gloriously overgrown and tagged with graffiti. They look like post-apocalyptic ruins, which, for the bears, they were. Atmospheric urban exploration without the trespassing.

name: Nantucket Lightship/LV-112
description: AI: A handsome red vessel that once marked Nantucket Shoals, now a small floating museum. Worth a look if you're already on the waterfront.

name: Royall House and Slave Quarters
description: One of the only surviving slave quarters in the northern United States, this small structure in Medford forces a confrontation with the myth that slavery was a Southern problem. Isaac Royall made his fortune on an Antiguan sugar plantation, then built this elegant mansion staffed by enslaved people. The main house is grand; the slave quarters are cramped and devastating. The guided tours don't flinch. Essential, uncomfortable history.

name: Old Schwamb Mill
description: AI: This Arlington workshop has made picture frames using belt-driven machinery since 1864, and almost nothing has changed. The same pulleys, the same lathes, the same wooden patterns. Watching craftspeople work here is witnessing the Industrial Revolution preserved in amber. Tours available; call ahead.

name: Ponyhenge
description: AI:  In a field in Lincoln, Massachusetts, someone left a rocking horse. Then another appeared. And another. Now dozens of plastic and wooden horses stand in eerie formation, rearranged by unknown hands, accumulating without explanation. No one claims responsibility. No one knows who adds to the herd or repositions them into new configurations. It's accidental art, collective weirdness, and the most inexplicably compelling site in Greater Boston. Just show up and behold.

name: Bonsai & Penjing Collection
description: AI: At the Arnold Arboretum, this collection of miniature trees includes specimens over a century old, shaped by generations of patient hands. The Japanese and Chinese traditions are both represented. Best in spring when the tiny maples leaf out, or fall when they turn.

name: Cyclorama
description: AI: This 1884 domed rotunda in the South End was purpose-built to display a 400-foot circular painting of the Battle of Gettysburg – an immersive Victorian entertainment predating cinema. The painting moved on, but the extraordinary space remains, now housing the Boston Center for the Arts. Stand in the center and look up at the dome's ingenious natural lighting. One of the strangest and most impressive interior spaces in the city.

name: The Fenway Garden Society
description: AI: During WWII, Americans planted vegetables to support the war effort. Most victory gardens vanished after 1945; this one never stopped. Seven acres of ramshackle plots along the Back Bay Fens, tended by a waiting list of Bostonians growing tomatoes where their grandparents grew tomatoes. The oldest continuously operated victory garden in America – living history you can walk through.

name: Massachusetts Historical Society
description: The oldest historical society in America (1791), holding Paul Revere's personal accounts, Jefferson's architectural drawings, and the Adams family papers. Not a museum – a working research library – but they welcome visitors and mount small exhibitions. For serious history devotees.

name: National Braille Press
description: AI: A working press producing braille books since 1927. Tours reveal the painstaking process of creating tactile literature. Niche but genuinely illuminating.

name: Temple Bell
description: AI: A 1675 temple bell in the Back Bay Fens, given to Boston by its sister city Kyoto. Pleasant if you're walking the Emerald Necklace.

name: Puppet Showplace Theater
description: AI: Brookline's intimate puppet theater has staged performances since 1974, and it's one of the few venues in America dedicated entirely to the art form. Not just for children – they program sophisticated work for adults too. If you've never experienced professional puppetry beyond Muppets, this is your chance. Check their calendar; a performance here beats most conventional theater.

name: Fort Warren
description:
Fort Warren is a historic fort on the 28-acre Georges Island at the entrance to Boston Harbor. It was constructed between 1833-1860 and was initially built as part of a broader network of coastal defense. The fort is named for Revolutionary War hero Dr. Joseph Warren, who sent Paul Revere on his famous ride, and was later killed at the Battle of Bunker Hill. Ferry ticket fares include round trip ferry passage to the park, plus any transfers to other islands.

Highlights
Here are some of the "must see" items at Fort Warren .

Fort’s Bakery
Parade Ground
Dark Tunnel

name: MassArt Art Museum
description:
AI: Massachusetts College of Art and Design has many different galleries on their campus. The Arnheim Gallery is a public venue used to showcase interfaces of art, education, and research. The Brant Gallery hosts cross-cultural exhibition programs, lecture series, and visiting artists. The Patricia Doran Graduate Gallery presents graduate student and student-curated events. The Frances Euphemia Thompson Gallery features curated exhibitions honoring distinguished members from the MassArt community. The Godine Family Gallery is a student-run multi-use space for exhibitions, performances, installations, conferences, lectures, events, and gatherings that serve the MassArt and Boston community. And finally, The Student Life Gallery presents student exhibitions throughout the year.

Highlights
Here are some of the "must see" items at Massachusetts College of Art and Design Galleries.

Nourish
Theresa-India Young
MassArt Thesis exhibition

name: Robert Gould Shaw and the 54th Regiment Memorial
Battleship Cove
description: AI: Utterly singular. Where else can you clamber through a WWII battleship, destroyer, submarine, and a Cold War Soviet-built vessel in one stop?

name: Beauport, Sleeper-McCann House
description:
AI: Wildly imaginative early-20th-century design — theatrical rooms, layered collections, harbor views. Feels like stepping inside a designer’s eccentric dream.

Verdict: Unexpected and deeply charming.

name: Peabody Essex Museum
description:
AI: One of the oldest and most important museums in the United States, founded in 1799. Its collections reflect Salem’s global trading history, with exceptional Asian art, maritime artifacts, and the remarkable transplanted Yin Yu Tang Chinese merchant’s house.

Why go: world-class museum rooted in Salem’s global maritime past.

name: Spencer-Peirce-Little Farm
description:
A rare surviving 17th-century farmstead with a massive stone house and surrounding barns and fields. The property offers a vivid sense of colonial agricultural life.

Why go: one of the most authentic early farm landscapes in New England

name: Castle Hill on the Crane Estate
description:
AI: One of the most spectacular historic estates in New England. The Crane Estate sits atop a hill overlooking Ipswich Bay, with a dramatic lawn stretching down toward the ocean. The Stuart-style mansion, formal gardens, and surrounding dunes create an almost European grand-estate atmosphere.

Why go: one of the most beautiful landscapes on the Massachusetts coast.
Must visit.

name: The House of the Seven Gables
description:
AI: Perhaps Salem’s most famous historic house, made legendary by Nathaniel Hawthorne’s novel. The 17th-century mansion features a dramatic gabled roofline and a secret staircase built into the walls. The waterfront setting adds to the atmosphere.

Why go: literary history and one of New England’s most iconic houses.

name: Ellisville Harbor State Park
description:
AI: quiet and scenic coastal preserve south of Plymouth with meadows, salt marshes, and a small beach. The walk down to the harbor passes through rolling fields with expansive views of Cape Cod Bay.

Why go: one of the prettiest lesser-known coastal parks in Massachusetts.

name: Great Brook Farm State Park
description:
AI: A charming park combining woodlands, ponds, and a working dairy farm. Visitors can explore miles of trails and finish with ice cream made from the farm’s milk.

Why go: idyllic New England farm landscape and great family stop.

name: Nickerson State Park
description:
AI: One of the best parks on Cape Cod. The landscape is dotted with clear kettle ponds left by glaciers, surrounded by pine forest and miles of bike trails. Swimming, kayaking, and cycling here feel quintessentially Cape Cod.

Why go: classic Cape Cod scenery with beautiful freshwater ponds.
Must visit.

name: South Cape Beach State Park
description:
AI: A stunning barrier beach park in Mashpee overlooking Vineyard Sound. Long sandy beaches, dunes, and salt marshes make it one of the most scenic coastal parks on Cape Cod.

Why go: pristine beaches and expansive coastal views.

name: Springfield Armory National Historic Site
description: The largest collection of historic military firearms in the United States.

name: Historic Arthur A. Smith Covered Bridge
Dr. Seuss National Memorial Sculpture Garden
description: A museum dedicated to the quirky and colorful world created by Springfield's favorite son.

name: Museum of Springfield History
description:
Hasbro Gameland
This exhibit is devoted to the games and wonder that Hasbro has brought children worldwide.

name: Whispering Giant
description:
At the back entrance to Forest Park, in Springfield, Massachusetts, there is a stylized bust of Omiskanoagwiah, the Wolf-People Medicine Man. It was carved from a single log by the Hungarian-born sculptor Peter Wolf Toth.

Omiskanoagwiah is part of the Trail of the Whispering Giants, a series of more than 60 sculptures that Toth created to honor Indigenous Americans. He has donated at least one sculpture to every state and several Canadian provinces. At one time, as many as 74 of these sculptures existed, but some have been lost to storms and other damage. Thousands of people drive past the sculpture daily, as the rear entrance to the park gives almost direct access to the nearby interstate highway. Most assume he is an image of the famous Metacomet, more commonly known as King Phillip, who led a bloody uprising against the English settlers of New England in the 17th century. Few of those passers-by know the story of how Omiskanoagwiah came to be part of their park.

name: Calvin Coolidge Presidential Library and Museum
description: A single room pays homage to the prodigious achievements of the 30th President of the United States.

name: Smith College Museum of Art
description:
Restroom Works of Art
Two artist-designed restrooms are part of the collection at the Smith College Museum of Art.

name: The Botanic Garden of Smith College
description:
'Plant Life Through The Ages'
A series of murals depict the evolution of plant life from the Precambrian to the modern day.

name: Mineral Hills Conservation Area
description: A rock and sand industrial site returns to its natural habitat.

name: Yiddish Book Center
description: A cultural center dedicated to the preservation of the Yiddish language and culture with over a million volumes.

name: The Eric Carle Museum of Picture Book Art
Stearns Steeple
description: The monumental steeple on Amherst College's campus has no church attached to it.

name: Beneski Museum of Natural History
description: This exhibit is one of the largest and most well-preserved collections of Jurassic-era trackways in the United States.

name: Emily Dickinson Museum
description:
Emily Dickinson's Bedroom
The mighty room where the poet spent most of her life is available to rent for an hour or two.

name: Amherst History Center of the Amherst Historical Society
description: The owner of one of the oldest homes in Amherst had a unique request before the home could be turned into a museum.

name: Rock House Reservation
description: A rock outcropping left by a glacier that made itself useful throughout the centuries.

name: Old Sturbridge Village
description: The largest living museum in the Northeast recreates life from the Early Republic period complete with costumed historians and reenactors.

name: Optical Heritage Museum
description: A quirky museum paying tribute to the history of the optical industry.

name: Naumkeag
description: AI: One of the great historic estates of New England, famous for Fletcher Steele’s dramatic terraced gardens, especially the iconic Blue Steps cascading down the hillside. The Gilded Age house itself is elegant, but the gardens—modernist, theatrical, and meticulously designed—are the real highlight. If you visit only one estate in the Berkshires, make it this one. The Blue Steps alone make this worth the trip—arguably the most photogenic garden design in New England. Terraced lawns, theatrical layouts, and Berkshire views give it a polished, almost storybook quality.

name: World's End
description: AI: A stunning coastal landscape of glacial drumlin hills overlooking Boston Harbor. Wide carriage paths wind through grassy slopes with constant ocean views and occasional glimpses of the Boston skyline. Designed by Frederick Law Olmsted, it’s one of the most beautiful coastal preserves in Massachusetts.

name: Royalston Falls
description: AI: A dramatic waterfall plunging through a forested gorge in north-central Massachusetts. Wooden staircases descend through mossy hemlock woods to reach the falls. It feels wilder than most landscapes in the state and is a standout natural site.

name: Tyringham Cobble Park
description: AI: A compact but spectacular Berkshire hike leading to a bald grassy summit with sweeping valley views. It’s one of the most picturesque viewpoints in western Massachusetts and surprisingly little-known compared with nearby state parks.

name: The Old Manse
description: AI:Historic house where Ralph Waldo Emerson and Nathaniel Hawthorne lived. The literary history, orchard gardens, and view of the Concord River make it one of the most atmospheric sites in Concord.

name: Mytoi Japanese Garden
description: AI: A tranquil Japanese-style garden hidden in the woods of Chappaquiddick Island. Small but exquisitely designed, with a pond, arched bridges, and winding paths.

name: Crane Beach
description: AI: One of the most spectacular beaches in New England. Miles of pale sand stretch along the Atlantic, backed by enormous protected dunes and maritime forest. Boardwalks lead through windswept grasslands to the ocean, giving the place a sense of wildness that’s rare on the developed Massachusetts coast. A must-visit coastal landscape.

name: Coskata-Coatue Wildlife Refuge Gatehouse
description: AI: A wild barrier-beach landscape of shifting dunes, salt marshes, and remote beaches at the northern end of Nantucket. Seals haul out along the shoreline, and the remote Great Point Lighthouse marks the tip of the island. One of the most pristine coastal ecosystems in the Northeast.

name: Vaillancourt Folk Art
description: studio producing collectible chalkware Santas

name: Horseneck Beach State Reservation
description: AI: A spectacular two-mile barrier beach on Buzzards Bay with huge skies and Atlantic surf. Less crowded than Cape Cod beaches and surrounded by protected coastal habitat.

name: Worcester Art Museum
description: AI: One of New England’s best museums outside Boston. The collection ranges from Roman mosaics to Impressionist paintings, and it once housed the famed Higgins Armory armor collection.

name: Mass Audubon Wellfleet Bay Wildlife Sanctuary
description: AI: One of Cape Cod’s best nature preserves. Boardwalk trails cross salt marshes, pine forests, and tidal flats rich in birdlife. Quiet, scenic, and deeply atmospheric.

name: Lynn Woods Reservation
description: AI: One of the largest municipal parks in the United States—larger than Boston’s Emerald Necklace. The woods contain miles of rugged trails, quiet ponds, and odd curiosities like Dungeon Rock, a cave associated with buried pirate treasure legends. It feels surprisingly wild for a park so close to Boston.

name: Coolidge Reservation
description: AI: A beautiful coastal preserve with sweeping lawns overlooking the Atlantic. The ruins of a once-grand seaside mansion add a slightly romantic atmosphere, and the ocean views are among the best on the North Shore.

name: Mass Audubon's Drumlin Farm
description: AI: A beautiful working farm and wildlife sanctuary operated by Mass Audubon. Trails pass through pastures, woods, and wetlands with views of classic New England farmland.

name: Codman Estate
description: AI: An elegant historic house known for its preserved 19th-century interior decoration, landscaped gardens, and scenic grounds along the Sudbury River.

name: Lowell Riverwalk
description: AI: A pleasant urban trail following the Merrimack River past mill buildings and canals, giving great views of Lowell’s industrial architecture.

name: Mass Audubon's Ipswich River Wildlife Sanctuary
description: AI: A beautiful Mass Audubon preserve with trails winding through wetlands, forests, and meadows along the Ipswich River. Boardwalks cross quiet marshes filled with birds and wildlife, making this one of the best nature sanctuaries on the North Shore.

name: Nantasket Beach Reservation
description: AI: A classic Boston-area seaside destination with a long crescent of sand facing the Atlantic. While developed, the beach offers excellent ocean views and is especially atmospheric at sunrise or sunset.

name: Mount Sugarloaf State Reservation
description: AI: One of the most famous scenic viewpoints in Massachusetts. The summit overlooks a dramatic oxbow bend in the Connecticut River surrounded by farmland and mountains. It’s an iconic Pioneer Valley landscape.

name: Oxbow National Wildlife Refuge
description: AI: A peaceful preserve along the Nashua River filled with wetlands, meadows, and forest. Boardwalk trails provide excellent wildlife viewing, especially birds and turtles.

name: Gibbet Hill
description: AI: A short but rewarding hike leading to wide views over Groton’s rolling farmland. The hilltop ruins of a small stone “castle” add a slightly romantic atmosphere.

name: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston
description:
AI: One of the great encyclopedic museums in the United States, with collections spanning ancient Egypt, Greek and Roman antiquities, Asian art, Impressionism, and American painting. The museum is vast but well organized, with particularly strong holdings of Monet, Renoir, Sargent, and Japanese art.

Highlights include the soaring glass-roofed courtyard, the Art of the Americas wing, and the atmospheric Egyptian galleries.

Why go: Boston’s premier art museum and one of the most comprehensive collections in North America.

name: Peabody Museum of Archaeology and Ethnology
description:
AI: One of the oldest anthropology museums in the United States, with extensive collections from the Americas and the Pacific. It’s academically important but the displays can feel somewhat traditional compared with newer museums.

Why go: Particularly strong for archaeology and Indigenous cultures.

name: Carpenter Center for the Visual Arts
description:
AI: America’s oldest nonprofit art association, exhibiting works by member artists in a traditional gallery setting.

Why go: Pleasant stop while strolling Newbury Street.

name: Retro Pop Shop
description: Journey through vintage Americana inside this small Massachusetts shop.

name: Chesterwood
description: Take a step inside the picturesque studio of America’s most renowned sculptor.

name: Clark Art Institute
description: AI: One of the finest small art museums in the United States. The Clark combines masterpieces by Renoir, Degas, and other Impressionists with a stunning modern campus set in the Berkshire hills. The museum grounds include walking trails and sculpture gardens, giving it the feel of a hybrid art museum and landscape park.

name: Mount Greylock State Reservation
description: Inspiring Herman Melville and Henry David Thoreau, Mount Greylock in western Massachusetts is the highest point in the state at 3,491 feet above sea level.

name: Becket Land Trust & Historic
description: Locals purchased this abandoned quarry in order to make sure it continues to be overgrown.

name: Natural Bridge State Park
description: Naturally formed white marble arch housed in an abandoned marble quarry from the 1800s.

name: Bash Bish Falls State Park
description: One of the most scenic falls in Massachusetts has a history of death and grim legend.

name: Hancock Shaker Village
description: Wander the sprawling living museum on the site of one of a 16th-century community.

name: The New England Peace Pagoda
description: This rare symbol of Eastern philosophy in the West has been created over years of painstaking construction by the local community.

name: Spruces
description: This abandoned neighborhood is now a park filled with beautiful trees, wildflowers, and hints of its past.

name: The Montague Bookmill
description: Books you don’t need in a place you can’t find.

name: Rock Fossil & Dinosaur Shop
description: This roadside attraction attracts kids with dinosaurs before blindsiding them with geology.

name: Mass Audubon's Pleasant Valley Wildlife Sanctuary
description: AI: A beautiful Mass Audubon preserve with forest trails climbing toward scenic viewpoints in the Berkshire foothills. Wildlife, wetlands, and quiet woodland hikes make it one of the best nature areas around Lenox.

name: Ventfort Hall Mansion and Gilded Age Museum
Boston Harbor Islands National & State Park
description:
A unique park made up of dozens of islands scattered across Boston Harbor. Ferries connect visitors to islands with beaches, hiking trails, historic forts, and panoramic skyline views.

Why go: a rare mix of wilderness and city views right in Boston Harbor

name: Borderland State Park
description:
A beautiful park of wooded trails, ponds, and the elegant Ames Mansion at its center. The property feels like an English country estate turned public park.

Why go: lovely scenery and historic estate atmosphere.

name: Bradley Palmer State Park
description:
AI: A scenic North Shore park of woodlands, meadows, and stone bridges built during the early 20th century estate era. Horseback riding and hiking trails wind along the Ipswich River.

Why go: peaceful landscapes and beautiful historic park design.

name: Mass Audubon's Allens Pond Wildlife Sanctuary
description: AI: A beautiful coastal preserve with barrier beaches, salt marshes, and nesting ospreys. Quiet and wild compared with most South Coast beaches.

name: Coast Guard Beach
description: AI: One of the most famous beaches on Cape Cod—often ranked among the best in the United States.

name: The Icon Museum and Study Center
New England Botanic Garden at Tower Hill
description: AI: One of the finest botanical gardens in New England. Perched on a hill overlooking the Wachusett Reservoir, the gardens combine formal plant collections, orchards, woodland trails, and sweeping views. The winter conservatory and seasonal displays make it worthwhile year-round.

name: Larz Anderson Park
description: AI: A beautiful hilltop park with sweeping lawns and views of the Boston skyline. The historic carriage house contains the Larson Anderson Auto Museum, one of the oldest car collections in the United States.

name: Fuller Craft Museum
description: AI: one of the leading contemporary craft museums in the United States.

name: Toys of Eros
description: this stimulating sex toy museum is sure to arouse the interest of its visitors.

name: Bob Gasoi Memorial Art Alley
description: Mural fragments and various sculptures honor the longtime artist.

name: Provincetown Portuguese Bakery
description: P-town goes wild for the malassadas at this 87-year-old institution.

name: Old Colony Tap
description: Pay homage to the quintessential P-town dive.

name: Three Sisters Lighthouses
description: These three lighthouses played a fundamental role in the maritime life of Eastham.

name: Doane Rock Picnic Area
description: The largest glacial erratic boulder on Cape Cod.

name: Captain Penniman House
description: The Cape Cod house that whaling built.

name: Cape Cod National Seashore Salt Pond Visitor Center
Hallet's Store
description: soda fountain from 1889

name: Scargo Tower
description: This lakeside tower is the third attempt at getting a tourist destination to stick on the spot.

name: Cape Cinema
description: The ceiling of this vintage movie palace is covered in fantastic Art Deco murals.

name: Edward Gorey House
description: Eclectic collections, artwork, and some feline friends fill the writer's former home.

name: Whydah Pirate Museum
description: This Cape Cod museum exhibits what it claims is the only authenticated pirate treasure in the world.

name: Red Maple Swamp Trail
description: Boardwalk sections of this trail meander through the heart of the Red Maple Swamp. This setting is the most colorful in the fall.

name: Garden Of Our Lady
description: Marigolds, rosemary, Madonna lilies, and the Virgin’s Bower decorate this Massachusetts sacred garden.

name: Lighthouse Beach
description: The Shack is a living beach sculpture on Chatham's South Beach, aka Lighthouse Beach, built of flotsam washed ashore by myriad storms. It is a place to sit, contemplate and enjoy the natural beauty of its surroundings. We hope it will endure awhile longer

name: The Knob
description:
A quarter-mile trail leads to the perfect spot to watch a sunset over Buzzards Bay. On a clear day, you can see the Elizabeth Island and New Bedford.

Walk the short trail from the parking area at the end of Quissett Harbor Rd for beautiful views. Please stay on the trails and respect this beautiful conservation land.

name: Stony Brook Grist Mill
description:
The Stony Brook Grist Mill & Museum is the only remaining structure from Brewster’s Factory Village, a once-thriving 19th-century industrial hub. This restored mill on Stony Brook Road is open every Saturday in the summer. Stop by to see the water wheel in motion and purchase freshly ground corn meal! After checking out the mill and attached museum, take some time to wander the footpaths along the brook to see a variety of wildlife.

In the spring, visit the brook to see the annual herring migration. From around mid-March into May watch the herring jump up the fish ladders of Stony Brook as they migrate from Cape Cod Bay to the freshwater ponds of West Brewster to spawn. Have you seen this spectacular sight? If not… be sure to add it to your Cape Cod bucket list!

name: Flying Horses Carousel a Vineyard Preservation Trust Property
description: The oldest platform carousel built in the United States continues to delight children in Martha’s Vineyard.

name: Back Door Donuts
description: Martha's Vineyard's most beloved speakeasy sells late-night pastries.

name: Nauset Marsh Trail
description: Amazing vistas overlook Nauset Marsh, and beautiful views of the Salt Pond.

name: Sandwich Glass Museum
description: This delicate museum is devoted to the art and industry that once supported Cape Cod's oldest town.

name: Heritage Museums & Gardens
description: AI: A Cape Cod classic, especially during hydrangea and rhododendron bloom. Large, varied, and easy to wander. Slightly more “family-friendly attraction” than pure garden, but still beautiful.

name: Nantucket Shipwreck and Life Saving Museum
description: A museum dedicated to Nantucket's legacy as the "graveyard of the Atlantic."

name: Capt. George Pollard House
description: The island home of an unlucky whaling captain whose story inspired a great American novel.

name: Maria Mitchell Hinchman House Natural Science Museum
description: Small island science organization offers public the chance to participate in research.

name: Greater Light
description: A pig barn converted into one of the most eclectic residences in Nantucket.

name: St. Paul’s Church of Nantucket
description: Mister Rogers Icon - Everyone's favorite neighbor is remembered fondly in this small-town church.

name: Whaling Museum
description: Artifacts of whaling, with both its perils and adventure, are housed in this museum in a former candle factory.

name: Sandwich Boardwalk
description: Hundreds of personalized inscribed planks make up this historic boardwalk.

name: Great Island Trail
description: Over 8 miles of trails with woods, marshes and beaches.

name: Aquinnah Cliffs Overlook
description: Colorful clay cliffs tower over an unofficial nudist beach on Martha's Vineyard.

name: Uncle Tim's Bridge
description: he footbridge is only the beginning of this really cool experience, and once you cross it, you’ll be on Hamblen Island, which has its own nature trails, and is a great place to spot some wildlife. This is a short walk from Mac’s On The Pier, a great outdoor seafood shack in town, as well as the shops in Wellfleet, making it an easy stop to make when exploring the Outer Cape.

name: Mayflower Beach
description: for tide pools

name: Blackstone River and Canal Heritage State Park
description:
AI: This park preserves part of the historic Blackstone Canal, a key transportation route during America’s early industrial revolution. Walking trails follow the canal towpath past locks and ruins.

Why go: excellent blend of nature and early industrial history.

name: Blackstone River Valley National Historical Park
Menemsha Hills
description: AI: A surprisingly rugged hilltop preserve on Martha’s Vineyard with sweeping views across Vineyard Sound. One of the island’s most scenic hikes.

name: Fruitlands Museum
description: AI: Transcendentalist utopian site founded by Bronson Alcott; spectacular hilltop views.

name: Sweet Heart Memorial
description: A tribute to the couples who brave long periods of separation during wartime.

name: Bartholomew's Cobble Reservation
description: AI: A remarkable limestone hill rising above the Housatonic River valley in the Berkshires. The cobble hosts rare plants and sweeping views across farmland and mountains. In spring the wildflowers are extraordinary. One of the most beautiful nature preserves in western Massachusetts.

name: Good Harbor Beach
description: AI: One of the most beautiful beaches on the North Shore. Wide sand, rolling surf, and views of Salt Island make it particularly photogenic. At low tide you can walk to the island across a sandbar.

name: Hammond Castle Museum
description: AI: eccentric medieval-style castle built by inventor John Hays Hammond Jr.

name: The Cultural Center at Rocky Neck
description: AI: one of the oldest art colonies in America

name: Historic Deerfield
description: AI: A beautifully preserved colonial village where historic homes line a mile-long street overlooking the Deerfield River valley. Many houses operate as museums, presenting early American life from the 1700s onward. Few historic towns in the U.S. feel this intact.

name: Lexington Battle Green
description: AI: One of the most important places in American history—the site of the opening shots of the Revolutionary War in 1775. The green, surrounded by colonial buildings, remains remarkably atmospheric. The nearby Minuteman statue commemorates the local militia who faced British troops here.
